# Psalm 56 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. According to The Dove on Far-off Terebinths. A Miktam of David, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.

**2** Be gracious to me, O God, for man tramples on me; all day long an attacker oppresses me;

**3** my enemies trample on me all day long, for many attack me proudly.

**4** When I am afraid, I put my trust in You.

**5** In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust; I shall not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?

**6** All day long they injure my cause; all their thoughts are against me for evil.

**7** They stir up strife, they lurk; they watch my steps, as they lie in wait for my life.

**8** For their crime will they escape? In wrath cast down the peoples, O God!

**9** You have kept count of my tossings; put my tears in Your bottle. Are they not in Your book?

**10** Then my enemies will turn back in the day when I call. This I know, that God is for me.

**11** In God, whose word I praise, in the LORD, whose word I praise,

**12** in God I trust; I shall not be afraid. What can man do to me?

**13** I must perform my vows to You, O God; I will render thank offerings to You.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 56.

- **56:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **56:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **56:9** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **56:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **56:13** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **56:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **56:9**: 'Put my tears in Your bottle' — one of the most intimate images in Scripture. God collects and preserves human tears. No grief is wasted.

### LOGOS
- **56:4**: 'When I am afraid, I put my trust in You' — trust doesn't eliminate fear; it coexists with it. This is honest faith, not denial.

### PNEUMA
- **56:5**: 'What can flesh do to me?' — Hebrews 13:6 echoes this. The contrast between mortal threat and divine power reduces human danger to insignificance.

— SOPHIA
